dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities match the stated purpose: list, search, export, create, update, and delete Apple Calendar events. These are sensitive calendar actions, but they are clearly disclosed and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions emphasize JSON output, stable calendar IDs, dry-run support for updates/deletes, and searching before mutation. Users should still require explicit confirmation before deletions, broad exports, or recurring-series changes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown-only and declares a global install of the external npm package @gopaljigaur/accli. The scanned skill does not include the npm package implementation itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: macOS Calendar Full Access can expose private calendar data and permit event changes, but that access is disclosed and proportionate for a calendar management CLI.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The only disclosed persistence is a default-calendar config file at ~/.acclirc, with override options. No hidden background worker, privilege escalation, or autonomous persistence is shown.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[SkillSpector] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues; artifact review did not find hidden or purpose-mismatched behavior.
[staticScan] expected: Static scan was clean, and the artifact contains only README.md and SKILL.md with no executable scripts.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry is pending and provides no artifact-backed negative signal.
[external-npm-install] expected: The global npm dependency is disclosed as the required CLI install, but users should understand this scan reviewed the skill instructions, not the external package code.
llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the @gopaljigaur/accli npm package and are comfortable granting it Full Access to Apple Calendar. Use narrow date ranges and calendar IDs, prefer --dry-run before updates or deletes, and require confirmation before deleting events, changing recurring series, or exporting broad calendar data.
llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Apple Calendar command-line helper, but users must be comfortable granting a third-party npm tool broad calendar access.
